# Animal Sounds

This site is the main documentation hub for the repository. It combines the project overview, workflow documentation, and the notebook-backed model comparison in one place.

The repository provides an end-to-end audio classification pipeline for animal vocalizations, including audio preprocessing, feature extraction, augmentation, training, evaluation, and prediction.

![](img/melspectrogram.png){fig-alt="Mel spectrogram example" width="70%"}

## What you can find here

- [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd): environment setup, data layout, and configuration file creation.
- [Training workflow](workflow.qmd): preprocessing, feature extraction, and training.
- [Prediction workflow](prediction.qmd): prepare new data, extract features, and run inference or evaluation.
- [Methods and data](methods.qmd): dataset summary, preprocessing choices, feature representations, and classifier details.
- [Model comparison](model_comparison.ipynb): rendered notebook with tables and plots.

## Project at a glance

- Two model families are supported: SVM for lightweight deployment and CNN models for higher-capacity learning.
- The pipeline was developed for chimpanzee vocalization detection and evaluated across distinct acoustic environments.
- Synthetic data generation is available to improve robustness on target-domain background noise.

## Software stack

- [Python >=3.12](https://www.python.org/)
- [Sklearn ~1.7.0](https://scikit-learn.org/)
- [Numpy ~2.2.6](https://numpy.org/)
- [Pandas ~2.3.0](https://pandas.pydata.org)
- [torch~2.6.0](https://pytorch.org) 
- [torchaudio~2.0.2](https://docs.pytorch.org/audio/stable/index.html)
- [torchlibrosa~0.1.0](https://github.com/qiuqiangkong/torchlibrosa)
